reforms.description: The April 1983 Federal budget included provisions to promote R&D expenditure and proposed the establishment of a 'national centre for productivity and employment growth' to address Canada's deteriorating productivity performance relative to other OECD countries.
reforms.component_name: R&D expenditure promotion and national centre for productivity
reforms.growth_orientation_rationale: Increased R&D funding and a dedicated productivity centre aim to reverse Canada's relative productivity decline and enhance manufacturing competitiveness, supporting long-term capital returns and investment.
reforms.status_evidence: The April 1983 Federal budget 'has taken further steps to promote R&D expenditure and proposes the establishment of a national centre for productivity and employment growth'.
reforms.importance_rationale: This is a system-wide initiative addressing Canada's structural productivity crisis through dual mechanisms: direct R&D funding increases and creation of a new national institution. It represents a major policy response to a critical economic challenge and signals sustained government commitment to innovation-led recovery.
reforms.source_quote: the recent Federal budget has taken further steps to promote R&D expenditure and proposes the establishment of a 'national centre for productivity and employment growth'.
